It is retreating in order, on ground it still holds, in front of an enemy it can still hurt. What has gone is the possibility of any outcome except a worse one later. The Americans came late and in smaller numbers, and it made a difference of months rather than of outcome. The request goes forward from the Supreme Command. It is a military judgment, made by soldiers, and within a few years a great many people who were in this building will say it was made by someone else.0MANPOWER ▾-5MUNITIONS ▾+1HOME FRONT ▾Settled recordChief of the General Staff at the close: Hindenburg. The war ends on the eleventh of November. Lorraine, August 1914: reinforced. The Marne: delegated forward under plenipotentiary authority. Two corps for the east: sent to East Prussia by rail. Ypres, November 1914: broken off. The eastern front, 1915: a breakthrough at Gorlice. Serbia: attacked in October 1915. The Meuse: fought as the directive was written. The Somme: ground given where it was dear. The Hindenburg Programme: adopted at full size. The submarines: held under prize rules. Weight of effort after the Marne: shifted east.
